w: King Harald V opened Norway's national aviation museum in Bodo on 15 May 1994, housed in a building shaped like a giant propeller. Covering around 10,000 square metres, it's the largest aviation museum anywhere in the Nordic countries, holding both civilian and military aircraft under one roof at the edge of the Arctic Circle.
s: A propeller-shaped museum of Nordic aviation
_facts: Opened by King Harald V, 15 May 1994
Largest aviation museum in the Nordic countries, ~10,000 sqm
Building shaped like a giant propeller
Holds civilian and military aircraft

w: This white stone church, raised in the long-church style around the year 1240, is one of the oldest buildings standing near Bodo. Seating about 300, it still serves as a parish church of the Church of Norway within the Diocese of Sor-Halogaland - a near-800-year-old survivor on the southeastern edge of town.
s: A stone parish church standing since around 1240
_facts: Built c.1240 in long-church style
White stone construction
Seats about 300
Parish church, Diocese of Sor-Halogaland

w: This 366-metre plateau above Bodo takes its name from Kaiser Wilhelm II, who supposedly climbed it on 19 July 1899, though whether he really made the trip is disputed. On a clear day the view stretches all the way to the silhouette of the Lofoten mountains across Vestfjorden. Stone stairs built in 2016 turned the climb from Bodo turisthytta into an easy walk, and the plateau now doubles as a concert venue during Nordland's music festival week.
s: A Kaiser's namesake plateau with a view to Lofoten
_facts: 366m plateau on Veten hill
Named after Kaiser Wilhelm II's disputed 1899 visit
View across Vestfjorden to the Lofoten mountains
Stone stairs built 2016; used as a concert venue

w: Built in 1956 to designs by architects Gudolf Blakstad and Herman Munthe-Kaas, this concrete cathedral in the long-church basilica style seats about 850 people. It serves as the seat of the Bishop of the Diocese of Sor-Halogaland and the church of the Bodo domkirke parish - a mid-century landmark for a diocese with roots far older than the building itself.
_facts: Built 1956, basilica-style concrete church
Architects Gudolf Blakstad and Herman Munthe-Kaas
Seats about 850
Seat of the Bishop of Sor-Halogaland

w: This 29.7-square-kilometre island sits right beside the Saltstraumen, one of the world's strongest tidal currents, connected to the mainland by the Indre Sunnan Bridge and to neighbouring Knaplundsoya by the Saltstraumen Bridge. Home to just 278 people as of 2016, it holds the Seinesodden Nature Reserve and the small village of Seines, whose exposed coast has made it a local surfing spot.
s: An island beside the world's strongest tidal current
_facts: 29.7 sq km island beside the Saltstraumen strait
278 residents (2016)
Seinesodden Nature Reserve
Village of Seines has a surfing spot

w: This 4.91-square-kilometre lake drains north of Bodo over the Valnesfossen waterfall on its short run down to the sea, sitting quietly beside County Road 17 near the village of Nygardsjoen. Unassuming compared to the fjords and peaks nearby, it's the kind of overlooked lake-and-waterfall pairing scattered across this stretch of the Nordland coast.
s: A quiet lake that empties over Valnesfossen falls
_facts: 4.91 sq km lake
Drains over the Valnesfossen waterfall to the sea
Lies beside County Road 17 near Nygardsjoen
